newsitem.title: GABON: Gabon's president in fresh Brazzaville talks.
newsitem.headline: Gabon's president in fresh Brazzaville talks.

text.p: Gabon's veteran president Omar Bongo on Friday began a fresh bid to persuade the Congo Republic's warring parties to end a showdown which has killed hundreds of people in their capital Brazzaville.

Gabonese officials said that Bongo, who proposed a truce which seemed to be holding in Brazzaville, had met representatives of President Pascal Lissouba and his rival and predecessor, former military leader Denis Sassou Nguesso.
Bongo also met members of a national mediation committee.

The fragile truce took effect on Monday. Bongo is spearheading international mediation efforts with U.N. and Organisation of African Unity special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun. Similar talks in June collapsed.

The conflict began in the capital of the oil-producing former French colony after soldiers surrounded Sassou's home as part of a crackdown on private militia ahead of a now-postponed July 27 presidential election.
Sahnoun says the aim of talks is to enable a presidential election to be held within the next two months. Plans for a U.N.-sponsored mainly African peace force are taking shape.

Shooting broke out in Brazzaville on Wednesday night but state radio there reported that rival fighters had met to bury the hatchet -- suggesting a celebration of peace progress. State television later showed the two sides fraternising.

Residents in Brazzaville said on Thursday that fighters from both sides, who have indulged in ethnic score-settling, were looting in areas under their control -- with hitherto untouched administrative buildings a target.
